mainTopic: Using one cup of wine for two separate מצוות: the rule that we do not do מצות חבילות חבילות
overview: This amud opens with רבי יוסי's ruling that after a meal that ran into שבת, one cup is used for ברכת המזון and a second cup for קידוש. The גמרא asks why one cup is not enough. רב ששת answers that two קדושות are not said over one cup, and רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that we do not do מצוות in bundles (חבילות חבילות). The גמרא first challenges this from a ברייתא where one cup serves both ברכת המזון and הבדלה, and answers that a person with only one cup is different. It then challenges from רב's order יקנ"ה for a יום טוב that falls on מוצאי שבת. It answers that since רב left out זמן, he must mean שביעי של פסח, when the wine has run out. That answer falls when אביי and רבא are shown to use one cup even on the first night, when there is plenty of wine. So the גמרא concludes that קידוש and הבדלה are one matter and may share a cup, while ברכת המזון and קידוש are two matters and may not. Finally, the גמרא turns to the dispute between רב (יקנ"ה) and שמואל (ינה"ק) about the order of the ברכות, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Two cups after the meal: one for ברכת המזון, one for קידוש
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי rules that after finishing the meal, the first cup is used for ברכת המזון and the second for קידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once they have finished eating, over the first cup a person says ברכת המזון, and over the second cup he says קידוש, the sanctification of the day.
steps.whatsHappening: This amud picks up the end of רבי יוסי's ruling: after a meal that ran into שבת, he wants two separate cups of wine, one for ברכת המזון and one for קידוש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each מצוה gets its own cup, and ברכת המזון comes first because the meal came first. This ruling is the base text that the whole passage will question and defend.

keyTerms.meaning: Sanctification of the day, i.e., קידוש

phrases.english: Once they have finished,
phrases.notes: Continues רבי יוסי's view from the previous discussion.

phrases.aramaic: כּוֹס רִאשׁוֹן מְבָרֵךְ עָלָיו בִּרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן
phrases.english: over the first cup one recites Grace after Meals
and over the second he recites the sanctification of the day.

steps.triggerLanguage: גָּמְרוּ, כּוֹס רִאשׁוֹן מְבָרֵךְ עָלָיו בִּרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier presentation of רבי יוסי's view, on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the meal, two cups are used: the first for ברכת המזון, the second for קידוש.

steps.title: Why not use one cup for both?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוסי needs two cups instead of saying both on one cup.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why? Let him say both of them over one cup!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבי יוסי's ruling and asks why two cups are needed when one could seem to do the job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברכת המזון and קידוש are said over wine, and they happen one right after the other. So using a single cup looks simpler. The question forces the גמרא to find a rule that requires a separate cup for each.

phrases.english: Why?
Let him say both of them over one cup!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for two cups in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's requirement of two separate cups
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One cup could serve both blessings, so a second cup seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Two sanctifications are not said over one cup
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא, quoting רב ששת, rules that we do not recite two קדושות over one cup.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said in the name of רב ששת: we do not say two sanctifications over one cup.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a general rule: two separate sanctifications are never said over a single cup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here "two קדושות" means two separate מצוה-blessings said over wine, such as ברכת המזון and קידוש. Because of this rule, רבי יוסי needs a second cup. The rule is stated here without a reason, and the next step asks for one.

keyTerms.meaning: Two sanctifications, meaning two separate מצוה-blessings said over wine

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read "two קדושות" as only two קידושים. ברכת המזון counts as one of the two here, even though it is not קידוש.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת:
phrases.english: Rav Huna said that Rav Sheshet said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אוֹמְרִים שְׁתֵּי קְדוּשּׁוֹת עַל כּוֹס אֶחָד.
phrases.english: One does not recite two sanctifications over one cup.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One cup could serve both ברכת המזון and קידוש.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two קדושות may not be said over one cup, so two cups are required.

steps.title: What is the reason for this rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב ששת's rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why two sanctifications cannot share a cup. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule was given without any logic behind it. Asking for the reason sets up a principle. That principle will later be tested against other cases.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason two קדושות may not be said over one cup.

steps.title: We do not do מצוות in bundles
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that מצוות are not performed in bundles.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: because we do not do מצוות in bundles.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives the reason: lumping מצוות together is improper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bundling מצוות makes them look like a burden that a person wants to get out of the way quickly. Each מצוה deserves its own attention, so each gets its own cup. This principle is now open to challenge from cases where one cup does seem to serve two מצוות.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule is אין עושין מצות חבילות חבילות: each מצוה gets its own cup so that it does not look like a burden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle has wide application across ש"ס. Whenever מצוות are combined, the question comes up whether they are being treated as a burden.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂין מִצְוֹת חֲבִילוֹת חֲבִילוֹת.
phrases.english: Because one does not perform מצוות in bundles.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מצוות are not done in bundles, because bundling makes them look like a burden.

steps.title: Challenge from הבדלה said on the ברכת המזון cup
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that someone with only one cup saves it for ברכת המזון and then says הבדלה on it. That looks like bundling.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do we really not combine them? But a ברייתא teaches: someone who comes home on מוצאי שבת makes a blessing on the wine, the light, and the spices, and then says הבדלה over the cup. If he has only one cup, he saves it for after the meal and strings all the blessings together after ברכת המזון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the no-bundling rule. It cites a ברייתא where one cup is used for both ברכת המזון and הבדלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the one-cup case, ברכת המזון is said on the cup, and then הבדלה and its blessings follow on that same cup. That seems to be exactly the bundling that רב ששת forbade. So the ברייתא appears to contradict the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: But was it not taught (in a ברייתא)?
The blessing separating שבת from the weekday
He strings them together, in a chain

phrases.english: And do we not?
But wasn't it taught:
One who enters his home at the conclusion of Shabbos

phrases.aramaic: מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַיַּיִן וְעַל הַמָּאוֹר וְעַל הַבְּשָׂמִים,
phrases.english: blesses over the wine, and over the light, and over the spices,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַר כָּךְ אוֹמֵר הַבְדָּלָה עַל הַכּוֹס.
phrases.english: and afterward recites havdalah over the cup.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא כּוֹס אֶחָד —
phrases.english: And if he has only one cup —
he leaves it for after the meal
phrases.notes: He uses it first for ברכת המזון.

phrases.english: and strings all of them together after it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the principle established in steps 3 and 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule אין אומרים שתי קדושות על כוס אחד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows ברכת המזון and הבדלה on one cup, which is bundling.

steps.title: Someone without a second cup is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא deals only with someone who has just one cup. That is a case of necessity.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where he does not have another cup, it is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the challenge. The ברייתא allowed one cup only because the person had no other choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The no-bundling rule still stands for someone who has enough wine. The ברייתא is an exception made because of lack. It does not show that bundling is acceptable in general.

phrases.english: Where he does not have [another cup], it is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the rule against the challenge of step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Limits the ברייתא to a case of necessity.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenge assumed the ברייתא applies even to someone who has two cups, but it is speaking only about someone who lacks a second cup.

steps.title: Challenge from רב's order of יקנ"ה
steps.stepSummary: On a יום טוב that falls on מוצאי שבת, a person has plenty of wine, yet רב rules יקנ"ה, which puts קידוש and הבדלה on one cup.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is the case of a יום טוב that falls right after שבת. There he has wine, and still רב said the order is יקנ"ה: wine, קידוש, candle, הבדלה, all on one cup.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge from a case where the person is not short on wine. The next step answers this challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The "no second cup" defense does not work here, because a person has wine on a יום טוב. Even so, רב combines קידוש and הבדלה on one cup. So the no-bundling rule seems contradicted again.

keyTerms.term: יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת
keyTerms.meaning: A יום טוב that falls on מוצאי שבת

steps.confusionAlert: יקנ"ה is a memory acronym for the order of the blessings, not a word. It shows that all four blessings are said on one cup.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.english: But there is a Festival that falls after Shabbos,
where he has [wine],
and Rav said: Yakneh (wine, kiddush, candle, havdalah)!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Renews the challenge with a case where the defense from step 7 does not apply.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule אין אומרים שתי קדושות על כוס אחד, as limited by step 7
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even where wine is plentiful, רב puts קידוש and הבדלה on one cup, which is bundling without any necessity.

steps.title: רב's case must be the seventh day of פסח, when the wine has run out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from רב's יקנ"ה. Since רב left out the ברכה of זמן (שהחיינו), he must be speaking about שביעי של פסח. By then the person has probably drunk all his wine, so this is again a case of necessity.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: Since רב did not mention זמן, we learn that we are dealing with the seventh day of פסח. Whatever wine he had, he already drank, and he has none left.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב ששת. It argues that רב's one-cup ruling is really about a person who has no extra wine, just like the one-cup case of the ברייתא (steps 6–7).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is that רב's list (יקנ"ה) has no ז for זמן. The only יום טוב night without שהחיינו is שביעי של פסח, because it is not a brand-new festival. After a week of meals and four cups, it is reasonable that the wine is gone, so combining is forced and is not 'bundling.'

keyTerms.meaning: The ברכה of שֶׁהֶחֱיָנוּ, said on the first night of a יום טוב
The seventh day of פסח. No שהחיינו is said on it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב actually said 'this is the seventh day.' The גמרא is inferring it only from the missing ז in רב's acronym.

phrases.english: They say: since he (Rav) did not say 'time' (Shehecheyanu),
phrases.notes: The missing ז in יקנה"ה is the clue.

phrases.english: we can infer that we are dealing with the seventh day of Pesach,
phrases.notes: The only יום טוב without שהחיינו.

phrases.aramaic: דְּכׇל מַאי דַּהֲוָה לֵיהּ אָכֵיל לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: when whatever (wine) he had, he has already consumed,
phrases.notes: Used up during the festival week.

phrases.english: and he does not have (any more).
phrases.notes: So it is a case of necessity, like the ברייתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 8 by limiting רב's case to a situation of necessity.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): רב's ruling applies when there is no extra wine.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's יקנה"ה shows that one may combine two מצוות on one cup even when plenty of wine is available.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב speaks of שביעי של פסח, when the wine is used up, so combining is done only out of need.

steps.title: On the first night of יום טוב there is wine, yet אביי and רבא still use one cup
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the answer in step 9. On the first night of יום טוב after שבת, wine is certainly available, and still אביי (יקזנ"ה) and רבא (יקנה"ז) put every ברכה, including זמן, on one cup.
steps.simpleTranslation: But on the first יום טוב, when he does have wine, אביי said: יקזנ"ה, and רבא said: יקנה"ז.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the 'he ran out of wine' answer. אביי and רבא combine קידוש and הבדלה on one cup even on the first night, when there is no shortage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי and רבא disagree only about where זמן goes in the order. Both agree that everything is said over one cup. Their rulings cover the first night, when wine is plentiful, so the need-based answer cannot explain why combining is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: The first night of the festival, when שהחיינו is said
אביי's order: יין, קידוש, זמן, נר, הבדלה
רבא's order: יין, קידוש, נר, הבדלה, זמן

steps.confusionAlert: אביי and רבא are not arguing about whether to use one cup. They both use one cup. They argue only about the position of זמן.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא יוֹם טוֹב רִאשׁוֹן דְּאִית לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: But there is the first Yom Tov, when he does have (wine),
phrases.notes: No shortage of wine on the first night.

phrases.english: and Abaye said: wine, kiddush, time, candle, havdalah,
and Rava said: wine, kiddush, candle, havdalah, time.
phrases.notes: זמן comes last. Either way, everything is on one cup.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא יוֹם טוֹב רִאשׁוֹן דְּאִית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Knocks down the answer of step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that combining on one cup happens only when there is no extra wine.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אביי and רבא combine קידוש and הבדלה on one cup on the first night, when wine is surely available. So the combining is not driven by need, and the problem of 'bundling' returns.

steps.title: קידוש and הבדלה are one matter; ברכת המזון and קידוש are two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new answer. Combining קידוש and הבדלה is not 'bundling,' because both are a single kind of מצוה‎. ברכת המזון and קידוש are two unrelated מצוות, so רב ששת forbids combining them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: הבדלה and קידוש are one matter. ברכת המזון and קידוש are two matters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the 'shortage of wine' answer and replaces it with a new way to explain רב ששת's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule against חבילות חבילות only applies to two different מצוות‎. קידוש and הבדלה both declare the holiness of the day, so together they count as one מצוה‎. ברכת המזון thanks ה׳ for food and has nothing to do with קידוש, so putting them on one cup is real bundling.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the previous answer is being dropped
One matter / one kind of thing

steps.whatToRemember: The ban on 'bundling' מצוות applies only to unrelated מצוות‎. קידוש and הבדלה count as one theme, so they may share a cup. ברכת המזון and קידוש are two themes, so they may not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the boundary of אין עושין מצוות חבילות חבילות. What matters is whether the מצוות share a single theme, not whether there is a shortage.

phrases.english: Rather: havdalah and kiddush
phrases.notes: The answer of step 9 is set aside.

phrases.english: are one matter,
phrases.notes: Both mark the holiness of the day.

phrases.english: Grace after meals and kiddush
phrases.notes: This was the case of רב ששת.

phrases.english: are two (separate) matters.
phrases.notes: So combining them is forbidden bundling.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: הַבְדָּלָה וְקִידּוּשׁ חֲדָא מִילְּתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 9 with a new distinction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Conceptual distinction: related מצוות versus unrelated מצוות.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any two מצוות on one cup count as bundling, unless there is a shortage of wine.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only unrelated מצוות count as bundling. קידוש and הבדלה are one theme and may share a cup.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב ששת's ban applies to ברכת המזון with קידוש, not to קידוש with הבדלה.

steps.title: The original dispute: רב says יקנ"ה, שמואל says ינה"ק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now returns to the original statement it quoted earlier. When יום טוב falls on מוצאי שבת, רב's order is יקנ"ה and שמואל's order is ינה"ק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: When יום טוב falls after שבת, רב says: יקנה"ה. שמואל says: ינה"ק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section. It goes back to the dispute about the order of ברכות that it borrowed earlier for its challenge, and it is setting up a discussion of that dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב puts קידוש first, right after the wine, and then נר and הבדלה. שמואל puts נר and הבדלה first and קידוש last. Both agree that all the ברכות go on one cup. They disagree only about which comes first, קידוש or הבדלה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself.' The גמרא returns to a statement it quoted in passing
רב's order: יין, קידוש, נר, הבדלה
שמואל's order: יין, נר, הבדלה, קידוש

steps.confusionAlert: The letters stand for ברכות: י = יין, ק = קידוש, נ = נר, ה = הבדלה, ז = זמן. The order of the letters is the order of the ברכות.

phrases.english: The matter itself:
phrases.notes: The גמרא returns to the source it quoted in step 8.

phrases.aramaic: יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.english: A Yom Tov that falls after Shabbat,
Rav said: wine, kiddush, candle, havdalah.
And Shmuel said: wine, candle, havdalah, kiddush.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא. יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רב ששת discussion and opens an analysis of the רב and שמואל dispute that was quoted in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When יום טוב falls on מוצאי שבת, רב orders the ברכות יין, קידוש, נר, הבדלה, and שמואל orders them יין, נר, הבדלה, קידוש.
